# Retained teacher references for CPU tests

The 17 `.txt` files derive from 322,134 reviewed original bytes. Eleven bodies
remain byte-identical. Six replace only 26 private home-path prefixes with
`/home/<user>` and one private workspace prefix with `<workspace>`.
`manifest.json` separates original SHA256/byte counts from fixture SHA256/byte
counts and declares each substitution count. This includes the retained
owner guard, priority/readiness loop, SQLite checkpoint/recovery, Companion,
private-process cleanup, Ceres history loader/publisher, encoder and adapter.

These files are CPU test and source-review evidence. They are not installed
production helpers or an authorization to load models, acquire custody, modify a
queue, or adopt a runtime. Neutral paths preserve the role of historical metadata
without publishing a maintainer's filesystem identity.
`tests/teacher_reference_fixture.py` validates fixture bytes, then
materializes them in pytest-owned directories and derives explicit unqualified
CPU metadata. Readiness namespaces and native/runtime dependencies are relocated
by the fixtures. Fake-CPU subprocess tests use the pinned materialized fixture
bytes, including the unchanged original cleanup implementation. The shared
Ceres service accepts one exact neutral comparison digest only in its explicit
fake-CPU path; real-mode original source hashes remain unchanged.

The owner fixture projects only its loaded entry module's `sys.executable` onto
the resolved interpreter binary and pins that binary. This lets a CI venv alias
exercise the unchanged canonical-path/hash checker. Global interpreter selection,
venv prefixes, native hashes and production checker behavior remain unchanged.

The repository's own built native extensions and Python dependencies are still
required. No native binaries, models, training data or credentials are embedded.

The local `.gitattributes` disables text conversion for source `.txt` files so
Windows checkout does not change their byte hashes.
